run.question: We got a customer complaint about slow response times in Europe. The customer mentioned seeing request ID REQ-EU-8K4M2 in their error page. Find what happened with this request and which service had the issue.

report.summary: The request ID REQ-EU-8K4M2 could not be tied to any service: it does not appear in the only log store reachable in this Run, and the trace and metric backends that could hold it were unreachable (every Jaeger and Prometheus tool call returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE). The one region-labelled latency dataset available (Elasticsearch indices matching app-185-geo-*) shows a completely flat picture for the whole authorized window: 162 documents, all level INFO, every one with response_time_ms exactly 150, identically for eu-central, eu-west, us-east, us-west, ap-south and ap-northeast, and for all 27 services in that dataset; a range query for response_time_ms > 150 matched zero documents. That dataset's services (analytics, api, auth, billing, ...) are not the otel-demo deployments, so it is a different system and cannot be used to judge otel-demo latency. On the otel-demo side, all 21 deployments are 1/1 available and all 22 pods are Running, the node is Ready without pressure, checkout and payment logs show completed orders and charges through 09:07Z, and every flagd fault-injection flag is set to defaultVariant off, so no injected fault is enabled in that ConfigMap. All containers in otel-demo show a mass last termination at 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z (exit 255, reason Unknown) and restarted, and the otel-collector is spamming 'failed to upload metrics' against otel-collector:4318 (gRPC to an HTTP port) from its own internal-telemetry reader config; these are real but are not shown to be connected to the customer's latency report. Net: no affected otel-demo service can be named from this evidence, and the customer's European latency claim is unverified because per-service latency/trace data could not be read.

payment logs show each 'Charge request received.' matched by 'Transaction complete.' with a transactionId between 09:01:01Z and 09:07:21Z (last at 09:07:21.742Z, transactionId b26c4cba-e525-4b19-a3f0-12d73b61c4de), with no error-level lines in the returned sample.
The single cluster node opspilot-m1-control-plane is Ready with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure all False ('kubelet has sufficient memory available'), 8 allocatable CPU.

The flagd ConfigMap 'flagd-config' (key demo.flagd.json) defines the fault-injection flags productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad, and every one of them has defaultVariant 'off'.

Rejected: that an enabled flagd fault-injection flag (e.g. imageSlowLoad, adHighCpu, paymentFailure, cartFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) produced the reported slow responses for this request — in the ConfigMap actually mounted by flagd every flag's defaultVariant is 'off', so no injected fault is switched on there.

The otel-collector's self-telemetry misconfiguration (gRPC exporter pointed at otel-collector:4318, an HTTP OTLP port) is the mechanism behind the 'failed to upload metrics' log spam; this explains collector self-metrics export failures, not the reported end-user latency, and its traces pipeline still targets jaeger-collector:4317.

Because request-level records are unavailable (Jaeger unreachable, no request_id field in the Elasticsearch mapping), the identity of the service that handled REQ-EU-8K4M2 could not be resolved; the ID's format (REQ-EU-*) suggests an edge/region-tagging tier, but no object in the cluster emits that format in any log readable here.

gaps: Trace backend unreachable for the whole Run: traces_list_services, traces_search (frontend), traces_search_by_tags (frontend-proxy, error=true) and traces_query_trace_by_id all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span of REQ-EU-8K4M2 and no per-service/operation latency could be read.

Prometheus query API unreachable for the whole Run: execute_prometheus_instant_query, metrics_range_query, get_metric_names, get_all_labels, list_prometheus_rules and get_prometheus_target all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name,span_name,status_code}, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count and the kube_* series could not be examined; this is a gap, not a zero or a healthy reading.

The exact ID was not found: an Elasticsearch match_phrase on message 'REQ-EU-8K4M2' over all 1620 app-185-geo-* indices in the authorized window returned nothing; a match_phrase on 'REQ-' returned nothing; a match on message token '8K4M2' returned nothing. These queries returning nothing only shows those queries matched nothing.

The Elasticsearch mapping of the only log indices (app-185-geo-eu-west-catalog-2024.01.01) has fields @timestamp, level, message, region, response_time_ms and service and no request-id field, so per-request correlation is not possible from this store.

No Kubernetes events were found inside the authorized window (grouped by involvedObject.kind/namespace/reason the query returned nothing; 6 events with timestamps outside the window were dropped), so the cause of the 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z mass container termination (exit 255, reason Unknown) cannot be established and is not tied to the complaint.

Empty log queries (only 'this query matched nothing'): error-regex queries on cart, product-catalog, ad and recommendation returned no matching lines; the frontend and load-generator containers returned no log lines at all in the window; frontend-proxy retained only one line ('shutting down parent after drain' at 2026-11-22T08:19:46.111Z), so any access-log record of REQ-EU-8K4M2 there is unknown.

No per-region latency or error metric for the otel-demo services could be read, so whether European users of frontend/frontend-proxy saw elevated latency is unverified; the flat 150 ms in app-185-geo-* belongs to a different application.

The prometheus-readonly-proxy nginx configuration is held in a Secret (secretName prometheus-readonly-proxy, mounted at /etc/nginx/nginx.conf) which cannot be read, so why the query path fails while the Prometheus server is ingesting could not be verified; the container has 6 restarts with last exit code 1.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so no deployment/config change record could be checked against the 08:04Z restart.
No timestamps or error-page details from the customer beyond the ID were provided, so the request's time of occurrence in the 24h window is unknown.
next_steps: Restore or validate the Jaeger query endpoint and the Prometheus read path (prometheus-readonly-proxy service on NodePort) so span and latency series for the incident window can be read; then look up the trace whose request ID is REQ-EU-8K4M2 and its span latencies per service.

Once Prometheus is readable, compare rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{status_code=~"[45].."}[5m]) and rpc_client_duration/rpc_server_duration percentiles per service_name between eu and non-eu windows to test the European latency claim.

Ask the customer/edge tier for the timestamp and the endpoint behind REQ-EU-8K4M2, and for the request-ID format owner (no cluster object emits REQ-EU-*), since pod access logs for frontend-proxy are no longer retained.

Review the otel-collector ConfigMap 'otel-collector' internal telemetry reader (endpoint otel-collector:4318 with protocol grpc) and point it at the OTLP gRPC port 4317 to stop the upload-failure spam.

Check who or what terminated all otel-demo containers at 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z (exit 255) using retained events or node-level logs, since the restart is currently unexplained and unlinked to the complaint.

content.relay:
connectors:
  spanmetrics: {}
exporters:
  debug: {}

    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] basicauth/prometheus
    endpoint: http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/otlp
    tls:
      insecure: true
extensions:
  basicauth/prometheus:
    client_auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] ${env:PROMETHEUS_COLLECTOR_PASSWORD}
      username: collector
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time

    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute

    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection

    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  - basicauth/prometheus
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - otlphttp/prometheus
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - redis
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - otlp
      - debug
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - periodic:
          exporter:
            otlp:
              endpoint: otel-collector:4318
              protocol: grpc
          interval: 10000
          timeout: 5000
